hunks.baseline: Just like the games I played as a kid, crossing an invisible boundary between two worlds had become a familiar process.
hunks.sol: Like the games I played as a kid, crossing an invisible boundary between two worlds had become familiar to me.

hunks.baseline: An unknown force would soon take hold of my consciousness and lead it somewhere, and at the end of that journey, the light of a new world would be waiting.
hunks.sol: An unknown force would soon take hold of my consciousness and lead it somewhere. At the end of that journey, the light of a new world would be waiting.

hunks.baseline: I sensed it instinctively. Even after the thought crossed my mind, the darkness didn’t fade. That was what startled me.
hunks.sol: I sensed it instinctively. What startled me was that even after the thought crossed my mind, the darkness remained.

hunks.baseline: The process and sensations that had grown as familiar as breathing felt strange now.
hunks.sol: The process, the sensations—both had become as familiar as breathing. Now they felt strange.

hunks.baseline: By all rights, my consciousness should have already crossed out of the modern world and into Murim.

hunks.baseline: Then I would recover my usual senses and consciousness in the other body I’d been apart from. It was practically a routine.
hunks.sol: By now, my consciousness should have crossed from the modern world into Murim. Then I would regain my usual senses and awareness in the other body I’d been apart from. That was the routine.

hunks.baseline: The darkness and silence that went on for what felt like an eternity.
hunks.sol: The darkness and silence went on for what felt like an eternity.

hunks.baseline: The pull that came at the end of that suffocating wait.
hunks.sol: Then, at the end of that suffocating wait, came the pull.

hunks.baseline: My consciousness was sucked toward some unfathomably deep place, as if it had collided with a massive tornado.
hunks.sol: As if caught in a massive tornado, my consciousness was sucked toward depths I couldn’t begin to fathom.

hunks.baseline: I clung with all my strength to the thread of my consciousness, shaken by a force of attraction more powerful than anything I’d ever felt.
hunks.sol: I clung with all my strength to the thread of my consciousness as a pull more powerful than anything I’d ever felt threatened to shake it loose.

hunks.baseline: If the previous trips had been limousines, this one was a locomotive.
hunks.sol: If my previous trips had been rides in a limousine, this one was a locomotive.

hunks.baseline: A runaway, broken-down locomotive hurtling down tracks that were rusted and out of alignment, with no engineer to control its speed.
hunks.sol: A broken-down runaway locomotive hurtling down rusted, misaligned tracks, with no engineer to control its speed.

hunks.baseline: A scream rang out in my mind before I could stop it.
hunks.sol: The cry rang out in my mind before I could help it.

hunks.baseline: But just as a school bully who was rotten to the core wouldn’t stop tormenting someone because of one short shout, the powerful wave carrying my consciousness somewhere didn’t stop either.
hunks.sol: But a school bully rotten to the core wouldn’t stop tormenting someone at a single shout. Neither did the powerful wave carrying my consciousness toward who knew where.

hunks.baseline: A shaft of light more intense than ever burst through the darkness as if tearing it apart, swallowing my vision.
hunks.sol: Darkness split apart as though torn open. A shaft of light brighter than any I’d seen before burst through and swallowed my vision.

hunks.baseline: Along with it came a voice, conveyed through my senses, which had all snapped sharply into focus.
hunks.sol: With it came a voice, carried to me through senses that had snapped sharply into focus.

hunks.baseline: He didn’t ask if I’d woken up.
hunks.sol: He hadn’t asked if I was awake.

hunks.baseline: He asked if I’d come back.
hunks.sol: He’d asked if I’d come back.

hunks.baseline: Leaving the frantic ordeal behind me, I slowly lifted my eyelids and looked at the owner of the voice.
hunks.sol: Leaving the frantic ordeal behind me, I slowly opened my eyes and looked at the owner of the voice.

hunks.baseline: Several bells were ringing loudly, starting with a System message announcing that Login had succeeded. But his voice washed over my ears like spring rain.
hunks.sol: Bells were ringing one after another, beginning with a System message announcing that Login had succeeded. But his voice fell on my ears like spring rain.

hunks.baseline: At the natural sound of that title, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, widened his eyes.
hunks.sol: At the ease with which the title came from my lips, the Fire King, Jeok Cheongang, widened his eyes.

hunks.baseline: And for that very reason, Jeok Cheongang must have noticed right away that something was wrong with me.
hunks.sol: And for that very reason, he must have noticed right away that something was wrong with me.

hunks.baseline: “You really can read minds. How’d you know?”
hunks.sol: “Are you psychic? How’d you know?”

hunks.baseline: It had soaked through my clothes and even the bedding beneath me. So much for having reached the realm of Unaffected by Cold and Heat a long time ago.
hunks.sol: Even the bedding beneath me was damp. So much for having reached the realm of Unaffected by Cold and Heat long ago.

hunks.baseline: “Just a little while ago. You were groaning so much I thought you might shit yourself.”
hunks.sol: “A little while ago. You were groaning so much I thought you might shit yourself.”

hunks.baseline: Where had that warm, gentle feeling from a moment ago gone? Had I imagined the public-restroom stink in the air, too?
hunks.sol: Where had that warm feeling from a moment ago gone? Was it just me, or did the air smell like a public restroom now?

hunks.baseline: I grimaced and answered, “Hard to say. There are too many things that come to mind. Anyway, where’s everyone else?”
hunks.sol: I grimaced and answered, “Hard to say. More than one thing comes to mind. Anyway, where’s everyone else?”

hunks.baseline: No matter how I looked around, Jeok Cheongang was the only face I could see. And aside from the horses snorting as they galloped along, I couldn’t sense anyone nearby.
hunks.sol: No matter how I looked around, Jeok Cheongang was the only face I could see. And aside from the snorting of the horses pulling us along, I couldn’t sense anyone nearby.

hunks.baseline: The answer Jeok Cheongang gave me next made my already-prickling nerves go cold.
hunks.sol: His answer made my already-prickling nerves go cold.

hunks.baseline: I asked again, my voice trembling. “Gone?”
hunks.sol: “Gone?” I asked, my voice trembling.

hunks.baseline: “Ah, they’re gone! Right now!”
hunks.sol: “They’re gone! Right now!”

hunks.baseline: “To be precise, they all left about two hours ago. They had to scout around and find a place to camp tonight. They’ll probably be back soon.”
hunks.sol: “To be precise, they all left about one shichen ago. They needed to scout the area and find a place to camp tonight. They’ll probably be back soon.”

hunks.baseline: What the hell was that supposed to mean?
hunks.sol: What the hell?

hunks.baseline: I went quiet for a moment, then looked at Jeok Cheongang with a flat stare.

hunks.baseline: My heart had returned to its proper place long ago.

hunks.baseline: As Jeok Cheongang glared at me, I turned my head slightly to the side.
hunks.sol: As Jeok Cheongang glared at me, I turned my head toward the window.

hunks.baseline: Outside the window of the magnificent eight-horse carriage the emperor of the Great Nation—no, the Great Ming Empire—had sent just for me, the world lay shrouded in darkness.
hunks.sol: Outside the large, beautiful eight-horse carriage the emperor of the Great Nation—no, the Great Ming Empire—had bestowed on me alone, darkness covered the world.

hunks.baseline: The largest land in the world, a Land of Ruin that no one had dared invade throughout the ages.
hunks.sol: The vastest land under heaven, and a Land of Ruin no one had dared invade for ages.

hunks.baseline: While I’d been away from Murim, the journey that began in Qinghai had finally reached here.
hunks.sol: While I’d been away from Murim, the journey that began in Qinghai had finally brought us here.

hunks.baseline: Even now, grains of sand trickled through the gaps in the carriage, proving that we were in the heart of Xinjiang.
hunks.sol: Even now, grains of sand trickled through the gaps in the carriage, proof that we were deep in the heart of Xinjiang.

hunks.baseline: “Taklamakan Desert.”
hunks.sol: “The Taklamakan Desert.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang muttered the name under his breath, then spat out the sand in his mouth.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang muttered the name, then spat out the sand that had gotten into his mouth.

hunks.baseline: “Damn desert. After all the hell I’ve been through for nearly a month, I really…”
hunks.sol: “Damn desert. When I think of all the hell I’ve been through for nearly a month, I really…”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t hear the rest of what he said.
hunks.sol: I didn’t hear the rest.

hunks.baseline: And yet a month had passed in Murim during those few days.
hunks.sol: Yet a month had passed in Murim during those few days.

hunks.baseline: *The flow of time has gone badly out of sync. Beyond the point of no return.*
hunks.sol: *The axis of time has gone out of alignment. Beyond the point of no return.*

hunks.baseline: Right after my battle with the Blood Lord in Qinghai, I’d realized the time ratio was seriously out of whack when I returned to the modern world.
hunks.sol: When I returned to the modern world after fighting the Blood Lord in Qinghai, I’d realized the time ratio was badly off.

hunks.baseline: But there was a difference between a sense of foreboding that existed only in your heart and one that had become reality.
hunks.sol: But foreboding was one thing when it stayed in my head. Seeing it become reality was another.

hunks.baseline: The cold ticking of the [Broken Pocket Watch] I’d tucked deep in my Inventory just before logging in seemed to ring in my ears like a phantom sound.
hunks.sol: The cold ticking of the [Broken Pocket Watch] I’d tucked deep in my Inventory just before logging in seemed to echo in my ears.

hunks.baseline: *But… on the other hand, maybe it’s a good thing that this much time has passed already. It means we’re that much closer to our destination.*
hunks.sol: *But… maybe it’s a good thing this much time has passed. It means we’re that much closer to our destination.*

hunks.baseline: But unlike the modern world, which had suffered terrible damage in just ten days since Morgoth’s arrival, there hadn’t been any significant damage here yet.
hunks.sol: Yet unlike the modern world, which had suffered terrible damage in just ten days since Morgoth’s arrival, this world hadn’t suffered any significant damage.

hunks.baseline: Or at least, it felt that way for now.
hunks.sol: Or at least, that was how it felt at the moment.

hunks.baseline: Who knew what things would be like once I’d finished asking this question?
hunks.sol: Whether I’d still think so after asking my next question was another matter.

hunks.baseline: “While I was asleep, did anything happen…?”
hunks.sol: “While I was asleep, did anything…?”

hunks.baseline: “You mean, was there any trouble? No.”
hunks.sol: “You mean, did anything happen? No. Nothing out of the ordinary.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation, as if he’d guessed what I was about to ask. His voice dropped lower as he added, “It’s so peaceful it feels strange.”
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang answered without hesitation, as if he’d known what I was going to ask. His voice dropped as he added, “It’s so peaceful it feels strange.”

hunks.baseline: “Just what I said. The sky is murky and impossible to predict. Snow and rain fall without warning, along with heat that could melt you and even hailstones. But aside from that, there’s nothing.”
hunks.sol: “Just what I said. The sky is murky and impossible to predict. One moment it’s snow or rain, the next it’s heat that could melt you, or even hail. But aside from that, there’s nothing.”

hunks.baseline: That wasn’t all that surprising.
hunks.sol: That wasn’t particularly surprising.

hunks.baseline: Besides, this was Xinjiang—the place where the Lord of Heaven had holed up—so if anything, the changes here would be worse, not better.
hunks.sol: Besides, this was Xinjiang, where the Lord of Heaven had holed up. If anything, the changes here would be worse, not better.

hunks.baseline: What caught my attention was the last thing he’d said.
hunks.sol: What caught my attention was the last thing Jeok Cheongang had said.

hunks.baseline: “Nothing at all?”
hunks.sol: “Nothing?”

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. On the first day, none of us noticed anything too strange. But it didn’t take long for everyone, including this old man, to realize.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. None of us thought much of it on the first day. But it didn’t take long for everyone, this old man included, to notice.”

hunks.baseline: And when Jeok Cheongang went on to explain, I realized there wasn’t the slightest exaggeration or lie in what he’d said.
hunks.sol: As he went on, I realized he hadn’t exaggerated in the slightest.

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang muttered in a low voice, then suddenly jerked his chin toward the window.
hunks.sol: Jeok Cheongang spoke quietly, then jerked his chin toward the window.

hunks.baseline: I frowned at the incomprehensible gesture, then let my words trail off.
hunks.sol: I frowned at the gesture, then stopped mid-sentence.

hunks.baseline: And in that instant, I understood.
hunks.sol: In that instant, I understood.

hunks.baseline: In the deep darkness, that vast, endless desert was filled with nothing but sand.
hunks.sol: Beyond the window, the vast desert stretched into the darkness, filled with nothing but sand.

hunks.baseline: At the same time, not a sound could be heard.
hunks.sol: And from that desert, not a sound.
